member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Accessibility.AccessibilityAdapter.QueryAXTree(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Accessibility.QueryAXTreeCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Accessibility.QueryAXTreeCommandResponse
member.summary: Response for Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Autofill.AddressUI
member.summary: Defines how an address can be displayed like in chrome://settings/addresses. Address UI is a two dimensional array, each inner array is an "address information line", and when rendered in a UI surface should be displayed as such. The following address UI for instance: [[{name: "GIVE_NAME", value: "Jon"}, {name: "FAMILY_NAME", value: "Doe"}], [{name: "CITY", value: "Munich"}, {name: "ZIP", value: "81456"}]] should allow the receiver to render: Jon Doe Munich 81456

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.RestartFrame(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.summary: Resumes JavaScript execution.

member.summary: Makes backend skip steps in the script in blackboxed ranges. Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings
member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.summary: If true, then `scriptSource` is allowed to change the function on top of the stack as long as the top-most stack frame is the only activation of that function.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Fetch.FetchAdapter.RequestPaused
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled and the request URL matches the specified filter. The request is paused until the client responds with one of continueRequest, failRequest or fulfillRequest. The stage of the request can be determined by presence of responseErrorReason and responseStatusCode -- the request is at the response stage if either of these fields is present and in the request stage otherwise. Redirect responses and subsequent requests are reported similarly to regular responses and requests. Redirect responses may be distinguished by the value of `responseStatusCode` (which is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) along with presence of the `location` header. Requests resulting from a redirect will have `redirectedRequestId` field set.

member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled with handleAuthRequests set to true. The request is paused until client responds with continueWithAuth.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Fetch.FetchAdapter.ContinueResponse(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Fetch.ContinueResponseCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Continues loading of the paused response, optionally modifying the response headers. If either responseCode or headers are modified, all of them must be present.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Fetch.FetchAdapter.GetResponseBody(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Fetch.GetResponseBodyCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Causes the body of the response to be received from the server and returned as a single string. May only be issued for a request that is paused in the Response stage and is mutually exclusive with takeResponseBodyForInterceptionAsStream. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior. Note that the response body is not available for redirects. Requests paused in the _redirect received_ state may be differentiated by `responseCode` and presence of `location` response header, see comments to `requestPaused` for details.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Fetch.FetchAdapter.TakeResponseBodyAsStream(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Fetch.TakeResponseBodyAsStreamCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a handle to the stream representing the response body. The request must be paused in the HeadersReceived stage. Note that after this command the request can't be continued as is -- client either needs to cancel it or to provide the response body. The stream only supports sequential read, IO.read will fail if the position is specified. This method is mutually exclusive with getResponseBody. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by major GC, which will show which functions cause large temporary memory usage or long GC pauses.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by minor GC, which is useful when tuning a latency-sensitive application for minimal GC activity.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings
member.summary: Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.InterceptionId
member.summary: Gets or sets the interceptionId

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.ErrorReason
member.summary: If set this causes the request to fail with the given reason. Passing `Aborted` for requests marked with `isNavigationRequest` also cancels the navigation. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.RawResponse
member.summary: If set the requests completes using with the provided base64 encoded raw response, including HTTP status line and headers etc... Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Url
member.summary: If set the request url will be modified in a way that's not observable by page. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Method
member.summary: If set this allows the request method to be overridden. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.PostData
member.summary: If set this allows postData to be set. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Headers
member.summary: If set this allows the request headers to be changed. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.AuthChallengeResponse
member.summary: Response to a requestIntercepted with an authChallenge. Must not be set otherwise.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandResponse
member.summary: Response for Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PageRanges
member.summary: Paper ranges to print, one based, e.g., '1-5, 8, 11-13'. Pages are printed in the document order, not in the order specified, and no more than once. Defaults to empty string, which implies the entire document is printed. The page numbers are quietly capped to actual page count of the document, and ranges beyond the end of the document are ignored. If this results in no pages to print, an error is reported. It is an error to specify a range with start greater than end.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.HeaderTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print header. Should be valid HTML markup with following classes used to inject printing values into them: - `date`: formatted print date - `title`: document title - `url`: document location - `pageNumber`: current page number - `totalPages`: total pages in the document For example, `` would generate span containing the title.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.FooterTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print footer. Should use the same format as the `headerTemplate`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PreferCSSPageSize
member.summary: Whether or not to prefer page size as defined by css. Defaults to false, in which case the content will be scaled to fit the paper size.

member.summary: Requests backend to produce compilation cache for the specified scripts. `scripts` are appended to the list of scripts for which the cache would be produced. member.summary: Identifies a document which the rule set is associated with.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Preload.RuleSet.SourceText
member.summary:
Source text of JSON representing the rule set. If it comes from `script` tag, it is the textContent of the node. Note that it is a JSON for valid case.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html - https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/blob/main/triggers.md

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Preload.RuleSet.BackendNodeId
member.summary:
A speculation rule set is either added through an inline `script` tag or through an external resource via the 'Speculation-Rules' HTTP header. For the first case, we include the BackendNodeId of the relevant `script` tag. For the second case, we include the external URL where the rule set was loaded from, and also RequestId if Network domain is enabled.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-script - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-header

member.summary: If executionContextId is empty, adds binding with the given name on the global objects of all inspected contexts, including those created later, bindings survive reloads. Binding function takes exactly one argument, this argument should be string, in case of any other input, function throws an exception. member.summary: Gets or sets the name

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextId
member.summary: If specified, the binding would only be exposed to the specified execution context. If omitted and `executionContextName` is not set, the binding is exposed to all execution contexts of the target. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextName`. Deprecated in favor of `executionContextName` due to an unclear use case and bugs in implementation (crbug.com/1169639). `executionContextId` will be removed in the future.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextName
member.summary: If specified, the binding is exposed to the executionContext with matching name, even for contexts created after the binding is added. See also `ExecutionContext.name` and `worldName` parameter to `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextId`.

member.summary: Specifies in which execution context to perform evaluation. If the parameter is omitted the evaluation will be performed in the context of the inspected page. This is mutually exclusive with `uniqueContextId`, which offers an alternative way to identify the execution context that is more reliable in a multi-process environment.

member.summary: Disable breakpoints during execution.

member.summary: Setting this flag to true enables `let` re-declaration and top-level `await`. Note that `let` variables can only be re-declared if they originate from `replMode` themselves.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.AllowUnsafeEvalBlockedByCSP
member.summary: The Content Security Policy (CSP) for the target might block 'unsafe-eval' which includes eval(), Function(), setTimeout() and setInterval() when called with non-callable arguments. This flag bypasses CSP for this evaluation and allows unsafe-eval. Defaults to true.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.UniqueContextId
member.summary: An alternative way to specify the execution context to evaluate in. Compared to contextId that may be reused across processes, this is guaranteed to be system-unique, so it can be used to prevent accidental evaluation of the expression in context different than intended (e.g. as a result of navigation across process boundaries). This is mutually exclusive with `contextId`.

The specified target is also auto-attached. This cancels the effect of any previous `setAutoAttach` and is also cancelled by subsequent `setAutoAttach`. Only available at the Browser target.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V125.Target.ExposeDevToolsProtocolCommandSettings
member.summary:
Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the following API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.summary: Defines how an address can be displayed like in chrome://settings/addresses. Address UI is a two dimensional array, each inner array is an "address information line", and when rendered in a UI surface should be displayed as such. The following address UI for instance: [[{name: "GIVE_NAME", value: "Jon"}, {name: "FAMILY_NAME", value: "Doe"}], [{name: "CITY", value: "Munich"}, {name: "ZIP", value: "81456"}]] should allow the receiver to render: Jon Doe Munich 81456

member.summary: Starts tracking the given computed styles for updates. The specified array of properties replaces the one previously specified. Pass empty array to disable tracking. Use takeComputedStyleUpdates to retrieve the list of nodes that had properties modified. The changes to computed style properties are only tracked for nodes pushed to the front-end by the DOM agent. member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.RestartFrame(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.summary: Resumes JavaScript execution.

member.summary: Makes backend skip steps in the script in blackboxed ranges. VM will try leave blacklisted scripts by performing 'step in' several times, finally resorting to 'step out' if unsuccessful. Positions array contains positions where blackbox state is changed. member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

Response for Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Fetch.FetchAdapter.RequestPaused
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled and the request URL matches the specified filter. The request is paused until the client responds with one of continueRequest, failRequest or fulfillRequest. The stage of the request can be determined by presence of responseErrorReason and responseStatusCode -- the request is at the response stage if either of these fields is present and in the request stage otherwise. Redirect responses and subsequent requests are reported similarly to regular responses and requests. Redirect responses may be distinguished by the value of `responseStatusCode` (which is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) along with presence of the `location` header. Requests resulting from a redirect will have `redirectedRequestId` field set.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Fetch.FetchAdapter.GetResponseBody(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Fetch.GetResponseBodyCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Causes the body of the response to be received from the server and returned as a single string. May only be issued for a request that is paused in the Response stage and is mutually exclusive with takeResponseBodyForInterceptionAsStream. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior. Note that the response body is not available for redirects. Requests paused in the _redirect received_ state may be differentiated by `responseCode` and presence of `location` response header, see comments to `requestPaused` for details.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Fetch.FetchAdapter.TakeResponseBodyAsStream(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Fetch.TakeResponseBodyAsStreamCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a handle to the stream representing the response body. The request must be paused in the HeadersReceived stage. Note that after this command the request can't be continued as is -- client either needs to cancel it or to provide the response body. The stream only supports sequential read, IO.read will fail if the position is specified. This method is mutually exclusive with getResponseBody. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by major GC, which will show which functions cause large temporary memory usage or long GC pauses.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by minor GC, which is useful when tuning a latency-sensitive application for minimal GC activity.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings
member.summary: Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.InterceptionId
member.summary: Gets or sets the interceptionId

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.ErrorReason
member.summary: If set this causes the request to fail with the given reason. Passing `Aborted` for requests marked with `isNavigationRequest` also cancels the navigation. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.RawResponse
member.summary: If set the requests completes using with the provided base64 encoded raw response, including HTTP status line and headers etc... Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Url
member.summary: If set the request url will be modified in a way that's not observable by page. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Method
member.summary: If set this allows the request method to be overridden. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.PostData
member.summary: If set this allows postData to be set. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Headers
member.summary: If set this allows the request headers to be changed. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.AuthChallengeResponse
member.summary: Response to a requestIntercepted with an authChallenge. Must not be set otherwise.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandResponse
member.summary: Response for Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.PWA.InstallCommandSettings
member.summary:
Installs the given manifest identity, optionally using the given install_url or IWA bundle location.
TODO(crbug.com/337872319) Support IWA to meet the following specific requirement. IWA-specific install description: If the manifest_id is isolated-app://, install_url_or_bundle_url is required, and can be either an http(s) URL or file:// URL pointing to a signed web bundle (.swbn). The .swbn file's signing key must correspond to manifest_id. If Chrome is not in IWA dev mode, the installation will fail, regardless of the state of the allowlist.

member.summary: Right margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PageRanges
member.summary: Paper ranges to print, one based, e.g., '1-5, 8, 11-13'. Pages are printed in the document order, not in the order specified, and no more than once. Defaults to empty string, which implies the entire document is printed. The page numbers are quietly capped to actual page count of the document, and ranges beyond the end of the document are ignored. If this results in no pages to print, an error is reported. It is an error to specify a range with start greater than end.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.HeaderTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print header. Should be valid HTML markup with following classes used to inject printing values into them: - `date`: formatted print date - `title`: document title - `url`: document location - `pageNumber`: current page number - `totalPages`: total pages in the document For example, `` would generate span containing the title.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.FooterTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print footer. Should use the same format as the `headerTemplate`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PreferCSSPageSize
member.summary: Whether or not to prefer page size as defined by css. Defaults to false, in which case the content will be scaled to fit the paper size.

member.summary: Whether or not to generate tagged (accessible) PDF. Defaults to embedder choice.

The url used is the url specified by the trigger (i.e. the initial URL), and not the final url that is navigated to. For example, prerendering allows same-origin main frame navigations during the attempt, but the attempt is still keyed with the initial URL.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Preload.RuleSet.SourceText
member.summary:
Source text of JSON representing the rule set. If it comes from `script` tag, it is the textContent of the node. Note that it is a JSON for valid case.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html - https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/blob/main/triggers.md

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Preload.RuleSet.BackendNodeId
member.summary:
A speculation rule set is either added through an inline `script` tag or through an external resource via the 'Speculation-Rules' HTTP header. For the first case, we include the BackendNodeId of the relevant `script` tag. For the second case, we include the external URL where the rule set was loaded from, and also RequestId if Network domain is enabled.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-script - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-header

member.summary: If executionContextId is empty, adds binding with the given name on the global objects of all inspected contexts, including those created later, bindings survive reloads. member.summary: Gets or sets the name

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextId
member.summary: If specified, the binding would only be exposed to the specified execution context. If omitted and `executionContextName` is not set, the binding is exposed to all execution contexts of the target. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextName`. Deprecated in favor of `executionContextName` due to an unclear use case and bugs in implementation (crbug.com/1169639). `executionContextId` will be removed in the future.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextName
member.summary: If specified, the binding is exposed to the executionContext with matching name, even for contexts created after the binding is added. See also `ExecutionContext.name` and `worldName` parameter to `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextId`.

member.summary: Specifies in which execution context to perform evaluation. If the parameter is omitted the evaluation will be performed in the context of the inspected page. This is mutually exclusive with `uniqueContextId`, which offers an alternative way to identify the execution context that is more reliable in a multi-process environment.

member.summary: Whether the result is expected to be a JSON object that should be sent by value.

member.summary: Whether preview should be generated for the result.

member.summary: Whether execution should be treated as initiated by user in the UI.

member.summary: Whether execution should `await` for resulting value and return once awaited promise is resolved.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.ThrowOnSideEffect
member.summary: Whether to throw an exception if side effect cannot be ruled out during evaluation. This implies `disableBreaks` below.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.Timeout
member.summary: Terminate execution after timing out (number of milliseconds).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.DisableBreaks
member.summary: Disable breakpoints during execution.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.ReplMode
member.summary: Setting this flag to true enables `let` re-declaration and top-level `await`. Note that `let` variables can only be re-declared if they originate from `replMode` themselves.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.AllowUnsafeEvalBlockedByCSP
member.summary: The Content Security Policy (CSP) for the target might block 'unsafe-eval' which includes eval(), Function(), setTimeout() and setInterval() when called with non-callable arguments. This flag bypasses CSP for this evaluation and allows unsafe-eval. Defaults to true.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.UniqueContextId
member.summary: An alternative way to specify the execution context to evaluate in. Compared to contextId that may be reused across processes, this is guaranteed to be system-unique, so it can be used to prevent accidental evaluation of the expression in context different than intended (e.g. as a result of navigation across process boundaries). This is mutually exclusive with `contextId`.

member.summary: Specifies the result serialization. If provided, overrides `generatePreview` and `returnByValue`.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Target.ExposeDevToolsProtocolCommandSettings
member.summary:
Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the following API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.summary:
Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the following API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Target.TargetAdapter.SetAutoAttach(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Target.SetAutoAttachCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Controls whether to automatically attach to new targets which are considered to be related to this one. When turned on, attaches to all existing related targets as well. When turned off, automatically detaches from all currently attached targets. This also clears all targets added by `autoAttachRelated` from the list of targets to watch for creation of related targets.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Target.TargetAdapter.AutoAttachRelated(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V126.Target.AutoAttachRelatedCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adds the specified target to the list of targets that will be monitored for any related target creation (such as child frames, child workers and new versions of service worker) and reported through `attachedToTarget`. The specified target is also auto-attached. This cancels the effect of any previous `setAutoAttach` and is also cancelled by subsequent `setAutoAttach`. Only available at the Browser target.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Accessibility.AccessibilityAdapter.QueryAXTree(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Accessibility.QueryAXTreeCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Accessibility.QueryAXTreeCommandSettings
member.summary: Query a DOM node's accessibility subtree for accessible name and role. This command computes the name and role for all nodes in the subtree, including those that are ignored for accessibility, and returns those that match the specified name and role. If no DOM node is specified, or the DOM node does not exist, the command returns an error. If neither `accessibleName` or `role` is specified, it returns all the accessibility nodes in the subtree.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Autofill.AddressUI
member.summary: Defines how an address can be displayed like in chrome://settings/addresses. Address UI is a two dimensional array, each inner array is an "address information line", and when rendered in a UI surface should be displayed as such. The following address UI for instance: [[{name: "GIVE_NAME", value: "Jon"}, {name: "FAMILY_NAME", value: "Doe"}], [{name: "CITY", value: "Munich"}, {name: "ZIP", value: "81456"}]] should allow the receiver to render: Jon Doe Munich 81456

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.RemoveBreakpoint(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.RemoveBreakpointCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.RestartFrame(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.summary: Resumes JavaScript execution.

member.summary: Searches for given string in script content.

member.summary: Replace previous blackbox patterns with passed ones. Forces backend to skip stepping/pausing in scripts with url matching one of the patterns. VM will try to leave blackboxed script by performing 'step in' several times, finally resorting to 'step out' if unsuccessful.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.DebuggerAdapter.SetBlackboxedRanges(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.SetBlackboxedRangesCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Makes backend skip steps in the script in blackboxed ranges. VM will try leave blacklisted scripts by performing 'step in' several times, finally resorting to 'step out' if unsuccessful. Positions array contains positions where blackbox state is changed. First interval isn't blackboxed. Array should be sorted.

member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings
member.summary:
Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.CallFrameId
member.summary: Call frame identifier to evaluate on.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandSettings.Mode
member.summary: The `mode` parameter must be present and set to 'StepInto', otherwise `restartFrame` will error out.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.RestartFrameCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Restarts particular call frame from the beginning. The old, deprecated behavior of `restartFrame` is to stay paused and allow further CDP commands after a restart was scheduled. This can cause problems with restarting, so we now continue execution immediatly after it has been scheduled until we reach the beginning of the restarted frame.
To stay back-wards compatible, `restartFrame` now expects a `mode` parameter to be present. If the `mode` parameter is missing, `restartFrame` errors out.
The various return values are deprecated and `callFrames` is always empty. Use the call frames from the `Debugger#paused` events instead, that fires once V8 pauses at the beginning of the restarted function.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings
member.summary:
Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.ScriptId
member.summary: Id of the script to edit.

member.summary: New content of the script.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.DryRun
member.summary: If true the change will not actually be applied. Dry run may be used to get result description without actually modifying the code.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandSettings.AllowTopFrameEditing
member.summary: If true, then `scriptSource` is allowed to change the function on top of the stack as long as the top-most stack frame is the only activation of that function.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Debugger.SetScriptSourceCommandResponse
member.summary:
Response for Edits JavaScript source live.
In general, functions that are currently on the stack can not be edited with a single exception: If the edited function is the top-most stack frame and that is the only activation of that function on the stack. In this case the live edit will be successful and a `Debugger.restartFrame` for the top-most function is automatically triggered.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Fetch.FetchAdapter.RequestPaused
member.summary: Issued when the domain is enabled and the request URL matches the specified filter. The request is paused until the client responds with one of continueRequest, failRequest or fulfillRequest. The stage of the request can be determined by presence of responseErrorReason and responseStatusCode -- the request is at the response stage if either of these fields is present and in the request stage otherwise. Redirect responses and subsequent requests are reported similarly to regular responses and requests. Redirect responses may be distinguished by the value of `responseStatusCode` (which is one of 301, 302, 303, 307, 308) along with presence of the `location` header. Requests resulting from a redirect will have `redirectedRequestId` field set.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Fetch.FetchAdapter.GetResponseBody(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Fetch.GetResponseBodyCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Causes the body of the response to be received from the server and returned as a single string. May only be issued for a request that is paused in the Response stage and is mutually exclusive with takeResponseBodyForInterceptionAsStream. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior. Note that the response body is not available for redirects. Requests paused in the _redirect received_ state may be differentiated by `responseCode` and presence of `location` response header, see comments to `requestPaused` for details.

member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Fetch.FetchAdapter.TakeResponseBodyAsStream(OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Fetch.TakeResponseBodyAsStreamCommandSettings,System.Threading.CancellationToken,System.Nullable{System.Int32},System.Boolean)
member.summary: Returns a handle to the stream representing the response body. The request must be paused in the HeadersReceived stage. Note that after this command the request can't be continued as is -- client either needs to cancel it or to provide the response body. The stream only supports sequential read, IO.read will fail if the position is specified. This method is mutually exclusive with getResponseBody. Calling other methods that affect the request or disabling fetch domain before body is received results in an undefined behavior.

member.summary: Average sample interval in bytes. Poisson distribution is used for the intervals. The default value is 32768 bytes.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMajorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by major GC, which will show which functions cause large temporary memory usage or long GC pauses.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.HeapProfiler.StartSamplingCommandSettings.IncludeObjectsCollectedByMinorGC
member.summary: By default, the sampling heap profiler reports only objects which are still alive when the profile is returned via getSamplingProfile or stopSampling, which is useful for determining what functions contribute the most to steady-state memory usage. This flag instructs the sampling heap profiler to also include information about objects discarded by minor GC, which is useful when tuning a latency-sensitive application for minimal GC activity.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings
member.summary: Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.InterceptionId
member.summary: Gets or sets the interceptionId

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.ErrorReason
member.summary: If set this causes the request to fail with the given reason. Passing `Aborted` for requests marked with `isNavigationRequest` also cancels the navigation. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.RawResponse
member.summary: If set the requests completes using with the provided base64 encoded raw response, including HTTP status line and headers etc... Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Url
member.summary: If set the request url will be modified in a way that's not observable by page. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Method
member.summary: If set this allows the request method to be overridden. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.PostData
member.summary: If set this allows postData to be set. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Headers
member.summary: If set this allows the request headers to be changed. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.AuthChallengeResponse
member.summary: Response to a requestIntercepted with an authChallenge. Must not be set otherwise.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandResponse
member.summary: Response for Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

Not every requestWillBeSent event will have an additional requestWillBeSentExtraInfo fired for it, and there is no guarantee whether requestWillBeSent or requestWillBeSentExtraInfo will be fired first for the same request.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.NetworkAdapter.ResponseReceivedExtraInfo
member.summary: Fired when additional information about a responseReceived event is available from the network stack. Not every responseReceived event will have an additional responseReceivedExtraInfo for it, and responseReceivedExtraInfo may be fired before or after responseReceived.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.NetworkAdapter.ResponseReceivedEarlyHints
member.summary: Fired when 103 Early Hints headers is received in addition to the common response. Not every responseReceived event will have an responseReceivedEarlyHints fired. Only one responseReceivedEarlyHints may be fired for eached responseReceived event.

member.name: E:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Network.NetworkAdapter.TrustTokenOperationDone
member.summary: Fired exactly once for each Trust Token operation. Depending on the type of the operation and whether the operation succeeded or failed, the event is fired before the corresponding request was sent or after the response was received.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.PWA.InstallCommandSettings
member.summary:
Installs the given manifest identity, optionally using the given install_url or IWA bundle location.
TODO(crbug.com/337872319) Support IWA to meet the following specific requirement. IWA-specific install description: If the manifest_id is isolated-app://, install_url_or_bundle_url is required, and can be either an http(s) URL or file:// URL pointing to a signed web bundle (.swbn). The .swbn file's signing key must correspond to manifest_id. If Chrome is not in IWA dev mode, the installation will fail, regardless of the state of the allowlist.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.PWA.LaunchFilesInAppCommandSettings
member.summary:
Opens one or more local files from an installed web app identified by its manifestId. The web app needs to have file handlers registered to process the files. The API returns one or more page Target.TargetIDs which can be used to attach to via Target.attachToTarget or similar APIs. If some files in the parameters cannot be handled by the web app, they will be ignored. If none of the files can be handled, this API returns an error. If no files provided as the parameter, this API also returns an error.
According to the definition of the file handlers in the manifest file, one Target.TargetID may represent a page handling one or more files. The order of the returned Target.TargetIDs is not guaranteed.
TODO(crbug.com/339454034): Check the existences of the input files.

member.summary: Paper width in inches. Defaults to 8.5 inches.

member.summary: Paper height in inches. Defaults to 11 inches.

member.summary: Top margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.summary: Bottom margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.summary: Left margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.summary: Right margin in inches. Defaults to 1cm (~0.4 inches).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PageRanges
member.summary: Paper ranges to print, one based, e.g., '1-5, 8, 11-13'. Pages are printed in the document order, not in the order specified, and no more than once. Defaults to empty string, which implies the entire document is printed. The page numbers are quietly capped to actual page count of the document, and ranges beyond the end of the document are ignored. If this results in no pages to print, an error is reported. It is an error to specify a range with start greater than end.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.HeaderTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print header. Should be valid HTML markup with following classes used to inject printing values into them: - `date`: formatted print date - `title`: document title - `url`: document location - `pageNumber`: current page number - `totalPages`: total pages in the document For example, `` would generate span containing the title.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.FooterTemplate
member.summary: HTML template for the print footer. Should use the same format as the `headerTemplate`.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Page.PrintToPDFCommandSettings.PreferCSSPageSize
member.summary: Whether or not to prefer page size as defined by css. Defaults to false, in which case the content will be scaled to fit the paper size.

member.summary: Requests backend to produce compilation cache for the specified scripts. `scripts` are appended to the list of scripts for which the cache would be produced. The list may be reset during page navigation. When script with a matching URL is encountered, the cache is optionally produced upon backend discretion, based on internal heuristics. member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Preload.RuleSet.SourceText
member.summary:
Source text of JSON representing the rule set. If it comes from `script` tag, it is the textContent of the node. Note that it is a JSON for valid case.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html - https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/blob/main/triggers.md

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Preload.RuleSet.BackendNodeId
member.summary:
A speculation rule set is either added through an inline `script` tag or through an external resource via the 'Speculation-Rules' HTTP header. For the first case, we include the BackendNodeId of the relevant `script` tag. For the second case, we include the external URL where the rule set was loaded from, and also RequestId if Network domain is enabled.
See also: - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-script - https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/speculation-rules.html#speculation-rules-header

member.summary: If executionContextId is empty, adds binding with the given name on the global objects of all inspected contexts, including those created later, bindings survive reloads. Binding function takes exactly one argument, this argument should be string, in case of any other input, function throws an exception. Each binding function call produces Runtime.bindingCalled notification.

member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.summary: Gets or sets the name

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextId
member.summary: If specified, the binding would only be exposed to the specified execution context. If omitted and `executionContextName` is not set, the binding is exposed to all execution contexts of the target. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextName`. Deprecated in favor of `executionContextName` due to an unclear use case and bugs in implementation (crbug.com/1169639). `executionContextId` will be removed in the future.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.AddBindingCommandSettings.ExecutionContextName
member.summary: If specified, the binding is exposed to the executionContext with matching name, even for contexts created after the binding is added. See also `ExecutionContext.name` and `worldName` parameter to `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`. This parameter is mutually exclusive with `executionContextId`.

member.summary: In silent mode exceptions thrown during evaluation are not reported and do not pause execution. Overrides `setPauseOnException` state.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.ContextId
member.summary: Specifies in which execution context to perform evaluation. If the parameter is omitted the evaluation will be performed in the context of the inspected page. This is mutually exclusive with `uniqueContextId`, which offers an alternative way to identify the execution context that is more reliable in a multi-process environment.

member.summary: Whether the result is expected to be a JSON object that should be sent by value.

member.summary: Whether preview should be generated for the result.

member.summary: Whether execution should be treated as initiated by user in the UI.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.AwaitPromise
member.summary: Whether execution should `await` for resulting value and return once awaited promise is resolved.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.ThrowOnSideEffect
member.summary: Whether to throw an exception if side effect cannot be ruled out during evaluation. This implies `disableBreaks` below.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.Timeout
member.summary: Terminate execution after timing out (number of milliseconds).

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.DisableBreaks
member.summary: Disable breakpoints during execution.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.ReplMode
member.summary: Setting this flag to true enables `let` re-declaration and top-level `await`. Note that `let` variables can only be re-declared if they originate from `replMode` themselves.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.AllowUnsafeEvalBlockedByCSP
member.summary: The Content Security Policy (CSP) for the target might block 'unsafe-eval' which includes eval(), Function(), setTimeout() and setInterval() when called with non-callable arguments. This flag bypasses CSP for this evaluation and allows unsafe-eval. Defaults to true.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Runtime.EvaluateCommandSettings.UniqueContextId
member.summary: An alternative way to specify the execution context to evaluate in. Compared to contextId that may be reused across processes, this is guaranteed to be system-unique, so it can be used to prevent accidental evaluation of the expression in context different than intended (e.g. as a result of navigation across process boundaries). This is mutually exclusive with `contextId`.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V127.Target.ExposeDevToolsProtocolCommandSettings
member.summary:
Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the following API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings
member.summary: Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.CommandName
member.summary: Gets the name of the command.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.InterceptionId
member.summary: Gets or sets the interceptionId

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.ErrorReason
member.summary: If set this causes the request to fail with the given reason. Passing `Aborted` for requests marked with `isNavigationRequest` also cancels the navigation. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.RawResponse
member.summary: If set the requests completes using with the provided base64 encoded raw response, including HTTP status line and headers etc... Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Url
member.summary: If set the request url will be modified in a way that's not observable by page. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Method
member.summary: If set this allows the request method to be overridden. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.PostData
member.summary: If set this allows postData to be set. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.Headers
member.summary: If set this allows the request headers to be changed. Must not be set in response to an authChallenge.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandSettings.AuthChallengeResponse
member.summary: Response to a requestIntercepted with an authChallenge. Must not be set otherwise.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Network.ContinueInterceptedRequestCommandResponse
member.summary: Response for Response to Network.requestIntercepted which either modifies the request to continue with any modifications, or blocks it, or completes it with the provided response bytes. If a network fetch occurs as a result which encounters a redirect an additional Network.requestIntercepted event will be sent with the same InterceptionId. Deprecated, use Fetch.continueRequest, Fetch.fulfillRequest and Fetch.failRequest instead.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.DevTools.V85.Target.ExposeDevToolsProtocolCommandSettings
member.summary:
Inject object to the target's main frame that provides a communication channel with browser target.
Injected object will be available as `window[bindingName]`.
The object has the follwing API: - `binding.send(json)` - a method to send messages over the remote debugging protocol - `binding.onmessage = json => handleMessage(json)` - a callback that will be called for the protocol notifications and command responses.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.DriverOptions.ImplicitWaitTimeout
member.summary: Gets or sets the implicit wait timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when searching for an element if it is not immediately present.
member.remarks:
When searching for a single element, the driver should poll the page until the element has been found, or this timeout expires before throwing a . When searching for multiple elements, the driver should poll the page until at least one element has been found or this timeout has expired.
Increasing the implicit wait timeout should be used judiciously as it will have an adverse effect on test run time, especially when used with slower location strategies like XPath.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.Firefox.FirefoxDriver
member.summary: Provides a way to access Firefox to run tests.
member.remarks:
When the FirefoxDriver object has been instantiated the browser will load. The test can then navigate to the URL under test and start your test.
In the case of the FirefoxDriver, you can specify a named profile to be used, or you can let the driver create a temporary, anonymous profile. A custom extension allowing the driver to communicate to the browser will be installed into the profile.

member.summary: Gets or sets the implicit wait timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when searching for an element if it is not immediately present.
member.remarks:
When searching for a single element, the driver should poll the page until the element has been found, or this timeout expires before throwing a . When searching for multiple elements, the driver should poll the page until at least one element has been found or this timeout has expired.
Increasing the implicit wait timeout should be used judiciously as it will have an adverse effect on test run time, especially when used with slower location strategies like XPath.

member.name: T:OpenQA.Selenium.IWebDriver
member.summary: Defines the interface through which the user controls the browser.
member.remarks:
The interface is the main interface to use for testing, which represents an idealized web browser. The methods in this class fall into three categories:
Control of the browser itself
Selection of IWebElements
Debugging aids
Key properties and methods are , which is used to load a new web page by setting the property, and the various methods similar to , which is used to find IWebElements.
You use the interface by instantiate drivers that implement of this interface. You should write your tests against this interface so that you may "swap in" a more fully featured browser when there is a requirement for one.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.IWebDriver.Url
member.summary: Gets or sets the URL the browser is currently displaying.
member.remarks: Setting the property will load a new web page in the current browser window. This is done using an HTTP GET operation, and the method will block until the load is complete. This will follow redirects issued either by the server or as a meta-redirect from within the returned HTML. Should a meta-redirect "rest" for any duration of time, it is best to wait until this timeout is over, since should the underlying page change while your test is executing the results of future calls against this interface will be against the freshly loaded page.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.IWebDriver.PageSource
member.summary: Gets the source of the page last loaded by the browser.
member.remarks: If the page has been modified after loading (for example, by JavaScript) there is no guarantee that the returned text is that of the modified page. Please consult the documentation of the particular driver being used to determine whether the returned text reflects the current state of the page or the text last sent by the web server. The page source returned is a representation of the underlying DOM: do not expect it to be formatted or escaped in the same way as the response sent from the web server.

member.summary: Gets or sets the width (magnitude on x-axis) in pixels of the contact geometry of the pointer.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the height (magnitude on y-axis) in pixels of the contact geometry of the pointer.

member.summary: Gets or sets the normalized pressure of the pointer input.
member.remarks: 0 and 1 represent the minimum and maximum pressure the hardware is capable of detecting, respectively.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.TangentialPressure
member.summary: Gets or sets the normalized tangential pressure (also known as barrel pressure) of the pointer input.
member.remarks: Valid values are between -1 and 1 with 0 being the neutral position of the control. Some hardware may only support positive values between 0 and 1.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.TiltX
member.summary: Gets or sets the plane angle in degrees between the Y-Z plane and the plane containing both the transducer (e.g. pen stylus) axis and the Y axis..
member.remarks: Valid values are between -90 and 90. A positive value is to the right.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.TiltY
member.summary: Gets or sets the plane angle in degrees between the X-Z plane and the plane containing both the transducer (e.g. pen stylus) axis and the X axis..
member.remarks: Valid values are between -90 and 90. A positive value is toward the user.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.Twist
member.summary: Gets or sets the clockwise rotation in degrees of a transducer (e.g. stylus) around its own major axis
member.remarks: Valid values are between 0 and 359.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.AltitudeAngle
member.summary: Gets or sets the altitude in radians of the transducer (e.g. pen/stylus)
member.remarks: Valid values are between 0 and π/2, where 0 is parallel to the surface (X-Y plane), and π/2 is perpendicular to the surface.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Interactions.PointerInputDevice.PointerEventProperties.AzimuthAngle
member.summary: Gets or sets the azimuth angle (in radians) of the transducer (e.g. pen/stylus)
member.remarks: Valid values are between 0 and 2π, where 0 represents a transducer whose cap is pointing in the direction of increasing X values, and the values progressively increase when going clockwise.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Timeouts.ImplicitWait
member.summary: Gets or sets the implicit wait timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when searching for an element if it is not immediately present.
member.remarks:
When searching for a single element, the driver should poll the page until the element has been found, or this timeout expires before throwing a . When searching for multiple elements, the driver should poll the page until at least one element has been found or this timeout has expired.
Increasing the implicit wait timeout should be used judiciously as it will have an adverse effect on test run time, especially when used with slower location strategies like XPath.
Also can be managed via driver option.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Timeouts.AsynchronousJavaScript
member.summary: Gets or sets the asynchronous script timeout, which is the amount of time the driver should wait when executing JavaScript asynchronously. This timeout only affects the method.

remarks.para: Also can be managed via driver option.

member.name: P:OpenQA.Selenium.Timeouts.PageLoad

member.summary: Gets the ID of the element
member.remarks: This property is internal to the WebDriver instance, and is not intended to be used in your code. The element's ID has no meaning outside of internal WebDriver usage, so it would be improper to scope it as public. member.name: M:OpenQA.Selenium.WebElement.GetAttribute(System.String)
member.summary: Gets the value of the specified attribute or property for this element.
member.param: The name of the attribute or property.
member.returns: The attribute's or property's current value. Returns a if the value is not set.
member.remarks:
The method will return the current value of the attribute or property, even if the value has been modified after the page has been loaded. Note that the value of the following attributes will be returned even if there is no explicit attribute on the element:
Attribute name Value returned if not explicitly specified Valid element types
checked checked Check Box
selected selected Options in Select elements
disabled disabled Input and other UI elements
The method looks both in declared attributes in the HTML markup of the page, and in the properties of the element as found when accessing the element's properties via JavaScript.
